abstract: Analyzing merits and demerits of the classic methods for the reconstruction of 3D circle and based the method for monocular reconstruction of 3D circle whose radius is known, we study the uniqueness proof and the matching principle for binocular reconstruction of 3D circle, further, present a new method for the binocular reconstruction of 3D circle whose radius is unknown. Our method is deduced fully based on the principle of imaging geometry and every step in the method is according to imaging geometry, thereby, it avoids the wrong solution which might happen in the Redundant Equation Error Method of the classic methods, and enhances the precision of the reconstruction. Experimental results indicate that the method can not bring any wrong solution which might happen in the classic methods, and is suitable for the reconstruction in the variable special instances and has high precision of the reconstruction.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ Filtering for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A full-order robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>filtering design for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems was investigated. The nonlinearities are modeled by neural-networks and then represented by linear difference inclusions. The uncertainties are described by polytope type. The presented filter is linear time-invariant, which not only guarantees the robust stability of error system but also satisfies a prescribed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>attenuation level for all admissible uncertainties. The sufficient condition for the existence of such robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>filter is provided in terms of linear matrix inequality. A simulation example is given to illustrate the design procedures.

articleTitle: Output Direct Feedback Control for Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a systematic design method of output direct feedback controllers for Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems. The direct use of the output measurements to produce the input signal to the controller avoids the requirement for measuring or reconstructing the entire state vector so as to decrease the complexity of the controller. In order to use the structural information in the rule base to decrease the conservatism of the stability analysis, the standard fuzzy partition (SFP) is employed to the premise variables of fuzzy systems. New stability analysis and design methods of output direct feedback controllers are presented and applied to a nonlinear mass-spring-damper mechanical system. The simulation results show that these methods are effective.

articleTitle: A New Searchless Fractal Image Encoding Method Based on Wavelet Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In this paper, an accelerating algorithm based on wavelet decomposition is proposed for fractal image encoding. Image range blocks are encoded based on fixed location domain blocks in different wavelet scales. Furthermore, encoding time can be shortened by utilizing the correlation between different wavelet scales. Simulations show that the compression ratio of our method is much higher than that of the searchless fractal method in spatial domain, while its runtime is short.

articleTitle: Set-observability of Control Systems with Limited Information
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A concept of set-observability is introduced for linear discrete-time systems in a network environment with limited data rate. Sufficient and necessary conditions on quantization level and observation precision are derived for set-observability. Data rates sufficient and necessary for the system to be finite time set-observable are obtained.

articleTitle: Synthetic-Output-Based Output Tracking for Nonlinear Non-Minimum-Phase Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A design of nonlinear output tracking control is presented for a class of non-minimum-phase systems based on synthetic output that is statically equivalent to the original process output and make the error system minimum-phase. Moreover, the nonlinear output tracking controller behaves with strong robustness

articleTitle: Flow Pattern Identification of Gas/Water Two Phase Flow Based on SVM
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Based on the conductance fluctuating signals measured from gas/water two-phase flow in vertical upward pipe, the 10 feature quantities, which reflect flow characteristics of gas/water two-phase flow, were extracted. The features in frequency domain were derived by using linear prediction method of speech signal processing and the features in time domain were derived by time series statistical analysis. The extracted features were combined with the experimental observed flow pattern information to establish the data set, and the support vector machine was used to identify the flow patterns of gas/water two phase flows. Finally the classification validity reaches 95.39% for the three type flow patterns of bubble, slug and churn. We conclude that the support vector machine is an effective method to identify the flow patterns of gas/water two phase flows at the condition of small sample data

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Subambient Pressure Air Bearing Under Nanometer Spacings in Hard Disk Driver
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Ultra-thin-film lubrication with nanometer spacings plays an important role in micro-scale fields such as MEMS, Hard disk drives. The usual methods of gas dynamics are no longer applicable when the mean free path of gas molecules is not negligible in comparison with the characteristic length of flow field. In this paper, a new model based on rarefied gas dynamics suitable to arbitrary Knudsen numbers is established firstly. Then, an effective numerical method is developed to calculate the modified Reynolds equation for ultra-thin gas film lubrication. The application to a typical case and numerical calculations using the modified Reynolds equations are performed with subambient pressure sliders. The numerical results show that the model and numerical method are valid for slider air bearing with nanometer spaces.

articleTitle: A Deadzone Modification for Learning Control of Time-Varying Uncertain Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a learning control method for time-varying uncertain systems, whose uncertainties are bounded by a parameterized function and the unknowns are assumed to be time-varying. A deadzone-modified iterative update mechanism to handle initial condition errors is incorporated in the control design, without assuming that the bound on initial condition errors is small enough in consideration of tracking performance. The resultant tracking error is shown to converge into a pre-specified deedzone, while boundednees of all the signals in the closed-loop learning system is guaranteed. The performance improvement is made possible by our design, due to the introduction of the width-deducing deadzone which boundary layer is governed by an initial rectified attractor defined based on constructive controllability analysis. The learning control method is also presented to deal with time-varying parametric uncertainties.

articleTitle: Optimum Study of Auto-disturbance-rejection Controller for High-order Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: An approach to design optimal auto-disturbance- rejection controller was presented for a class of observable high-order nonlinear plant. The controller parameters were optimized under the universal frame of genetic algorithms, and the desired dynamical equations were obtained according to the specified performance indices at the same time. A high-order plant was simulated using the method. Results were compared with the PID and exact feedback linearization control system. The results demonstrate that the method performs powerful functions for improving the dynamic characteristics. Simulation results also show that the method has good robustness against disturbances, noises and modeling uncertainties.

articleTitle: A Cone-Beam Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Nutating Line Filtration for Single Circular Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Traditionally, projection data are filtered along the horizontal lines on the detector plane for the FDK algorithm. This makes it impossible that the same voxels involved in the filtering at one projection angle are also filtered together at the other projection angles. To keep filtering together as much as possible for the same voxels at different projection angle, a cone-beam algorithm is presented based on the nutating line by modifying a result due to Turbell. Unlike Turbell's method, the proposed algorithm avoids the process step of rebinning the cone-beam data to 3D parallel-beam data. In addition, to further enlarge reconstruction volume and make the short-scan reconstruction, another FBP term suggested by Zhuang et al. is also modified into the final formula. The performance of the proposed algorithms is compared with other related algorithms through computer simulation using the Shepp-Logan phantom. The experiment results show that the proposed algorithm can substantially compensate for the low density drop inherent to the FDK-type algorithm

articleTitle: Guaranteed Cost Control for Chaos Synchronization: LMI Approach
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Based on Lyapunov stabilization and robust control theory, a guaranteed cost control law for synchronization of unidirectionally-coupled chaos systems is proposed in this paper. A linear model parameter uncertain form translation is given to transact the nonlinear part of the chaos system. Then, robust control is applied to the system. The optimal guaranteed control with linear error feedback scheme is solved by linear matrix inequality (LMI). A method to limit the control gain is also given to avoid great value. Finally, the effectiveness of the control law is verified and demonstrated by Chua's circuit and Lorenz system in numerical examples

articleTitle: A Model of Deceit-Tolerant Automated Negotiation for Open Environment
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Agent-based automated negotiation has been widely advocated to substitute human negotiation in the areas of electronic commerce and cooperative computing. However, deceptive behaviors in negotiation process may cause great harm to users' interests and hinder the practical application of automated negotiation. This paper presents a deceit-tolerant automated negotiation (DTAN) model, which copes with the deception problems in a tolerant manner to make automated negotiation more adaptive and robust in open environment. Inspired by the intelligent processing in the human negotiation, the DTAN model functions with cooperative works of four constituents: active deceit detection (ADD); deceit-sensed decision (DSD); deceit precontrol (DP); and subliminal self-protection (SSP). The frameworks and principles of the DTAN model are presented in this paper

articleTitle: The Study of Differentiated Products Pricing Strategy Based on Game Model
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The pricing strategy of differentiated products in two stages supply chain is studied in this paper. Using game theory, we build Nash game model, Stackelberg game model, and union pricing model. The optimal solution of differentiated products pricing strategy for manufacturer and retailer in each model is found. Based on this, the variety of supply chain total profits in each model is analyzed, and a valid pricing strategy set in union model is found. Finally, by computer simulation, we analyze the change of manufacturer's profits and retailer's profits in this three models, and reach a conclusion that total profits in union model are the best, Nash game model the next, and Stackelberg game model the worst. This conclusion is in accord with universal rule of economics

articleTitle: On a Sufficient Stability Condition for Ray of Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In this note, a sufficient condition for a ray of polynomials to be Hurwitz is established. The stability condition expressed in matrix inequalities is fit to be applied. The results established in this note can be applied to the problem of designing high-gain controllers and extends the results of a recent paper. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the results of this note

articleTitle: Combining Particle Filter and Active Shape Models for Lip Tracking
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm for lip tracking is proposed, fusing the strength of stochastic tracker and deterministic tracker. Particle filter and Active Shape Models (ASM) are used as deterministic tracker and stochastic tracker respectively. In order not to build complex dynamic model, we use deterministic tracker instead of stochastic tracker to estimate the local deformation part parameters of shape. Furthermore, to generate the initial optimal parameter sets of deterministic search, Resource Limited Artificial Immune System Clustering (RLAIS) is used, which avoids deterministic tracker searching for each sample. Our method improves experimental results considerably compared to particle filter, ASM or earlier hybrid methods.

articleTitle: Data Mining Method Based on HHT and Application Research in Flow Regime Identification
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: For identifying gas-liquid two-phase flow regime, a kind of data mining method based on Hilbert-Huang Transform was put forward. At first, the dynamic differential pressure signal coming from Venturitube was handled by HHT, the instantaneous frequency, instantaneous swing and user-defined characteristic variable of different mode were calculated. The relation of characteristic variable and flow regime was obtained by visual analyzing instantaneous frequency and characteristic variable. Afterwards, according to the distribution of characteristic variable, fuzzy association rules of identifying flow regime was gained adopting data mining method, and the results of flow regime identification were acquire through fuzzy illation and calculation. The experimental results of gas-water two-phase flow in vertical pipes with 50mm and 40mm inner diameter show, this method could identify bubble flow, slug flow and churn flow effectively, and discriminating precision exceed 94%. The method' principle is easy, has few influence by experimental condition and good universality, and it could settle for practical flow regime identification.

articleTitle: Design Architecture of Multiagent Control System
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: While multi-agent systems seem to provide a good basis to build complex control system, the variety of agent-oriented(AO) methodologies may become a problem for developer when it comes to select the best-suited methodology for a given application domain. To resolve the difficulties, a development architecture is proposed to blend various AO methodologies, which will pave the way for a unified and general AO methodology. We demonstrate the usage of the suggested architecture by combing two classes representative AO methodologies: KE-extended (knowledge engineering) method and OO-extended (object-oriented) method. By means of the combination, the method can provide straightforward connections between KE analysis results and OO software implementation. Finally, a case study is illustrated to show how to apply this method.

articleTitle: Bilinear Neural Network Tracking Subspace for Blind Multiuser Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In order to lower the level of multi-access interference (MAI) and improve the reception performance in CDMA communication systems, a new blind multiuser detection algorithm is proposed. Different from some other blind detection approaches, the proposed algorithm tracks the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of signal subspace by bilinear neural network based on a new principal component analysis (PCA) method. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm improves the tracking capability and bit error rate (BER) performance of blind detector compared with the MMSE and PASTd algorithm. In consideration of its comparatively low computational complexity, the proposed detection has some value in practice.

articleTitle: BNC Structure Learning: G2 Algorithm based Heuristic
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Structure learning for Bayesian networks classifier is NP-hard problem, K2 algorithm is one of efficacious and accurate algorithm. K2 algorithm confirms the order of nodes firstly. To a certain extent this limits in non-information. This paper purposes a new heuristic Bayesian networks classifier structure learning G2 algorithm. G2 algorithm use NB and TAN structure which learns as heuristic information, using K2 algorithm learning BNC structure. The experimental result shows that G2 algorithm can solve nodes order in non-information. Arcs are sententious, compare NB and TAN structure, it's more reasonable, classification accuracy improves, this algorithm adapts many aspects

articleTitle: Dimmable Control of Digital Electronic Ballast for HPS Lamps
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A novel micro controller-based dimmable electronic ballast for HPS lamps is presented in this paper. Power control method is based on the regulation of the average input current of the inverter by varying the switching frequency of the half bridge. Driver signal with low frequency modulation generated from MCU is used to eliminate unstable arc during dimming state. Theoretical analysis is discussed and experimental results based on a 600W HPS lamp show the feasibility of the proposed ballast

articleTitle: Research on Access Mechanism of WIRD Based on Object Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: From the analysis of workflow instance relevant data (WIRD), and a modeling method of WIRD based on object Petri nets is proposed. The method dynamically constructs an access mechanism of WIRD, to guarantee the security of WIRD. Moreover, a version management mechanism of WIRD is adopted as well as a collaborative communication mechanism of concurrent tasks is established to solve the inconsistency of WIRD during execution of workflow. The research of applied example has shown that this modeling method is significant in the application of access right and integrality of WIRD

articleTitle: Gene Name Automatic Recognition in Biomedical Literature
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Identifying gene names in biomedical texts is regarded as a crucial step for text mining. Our approach is a combination of dictionary based approach and machine learning based approach. Based on a gene name dictionary, an edit distance approximate string searching algorithm was used to improve the recall rate of gene recognition which is greatly lowered due to a lack of standard gene-naming conventions. Then the naive Bayes and SVM classifiers were adopted to filter out false recognitions, therefore improving the precision rate of gene recognition. The experiments show that classifiers greatly improve precision with slight loss of recall, resulting in a much better F-score (from 53.7% to 67.6%)

articleTitle: Application of Data Mining Methods in Eluxyl Process
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Eluxyl process is a simulated moving bed process. It achieves PX (paraxylene) separation from its other aromatic isomers. One year's historical data of Eluxyl process were studied, and data mining methods were introduced to extract useful operation information from them. Three main data mining procedures were discussed. Data preprocessing was discussed first. Then PCA (Principal Components Analysis) and K-means clustering technology were introduced and applied to discover different operational conditions in different loads. Finally fuzzy classification based on associations (FCBA) algorithm was used to discover the main reasons that lead to performance fluctuations and the rules denoting the typical operations.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ Filter Design with Sensor Fault
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a solution to a robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sub> filtering problem with sensor faults. The robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sub> filter design methods are developed against sensor faults. A given upper bound of the filtering H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sub> performance in the sensor faults case is guaranteed and the performance in the normal case is optimized. A new formulation in terms of linear matrix inequality (LMI) is adopted without introducing additional conservativeness. A flight control example is given to illustrate the proposed design procedures. Furthermore, the normal filter and the robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sub> filter are compared to show the necessity of robust design

articleTitle: Intelligent Simulation and Optimizing Control to Sprinkling Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: the contradiction between mutable operating condition and fixed design condition of sprinkling irrigation system is analyzed and intelligent simulation and optimizing control theory and method basing on computational intelligence is put forward. Basing on the water distribution obtained from sprinkling irrigation experiment of single nozzle under different work pressure and through computing motion equation of drip, water distribution under different work pressure and different wind speed is computed. Nonlinear relationship between work pressure, wind speed and water distribution is simulated by genetic BP neural network and computation method of uniformity degree of sprinkling irrigation under different nozzle's combination is put forward, and further more, genetic algorithm is introduced to optimize combination manner and space of nozzles. A simulation and optimizing control example is given at the end of the paper.

Author Keywords: combined uniformity degree of sprinkling irrigation

articleTitle: Low Power Design based on Neural Network Forecasting for Interconnection Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Power consumption is a key issue in high-performance interconnection network design. In interconnection network, power consumption of interconnection links will take up an ever larger portion of the power budget as demand for network bandwidth increases. Network traffic is an important factor that influences interconnection network power consumption. In this paper, we presented a traffic forecasting model using neural network method. Our interconnection network traffic forecasting model based on neural network adopted Back-Propagation learning algorithm and divided network period of time into two parts: stationary-hours and non-stationary-hours. Then we proposed voltage scaling algorithm for links based on our forecasting model. The results show that our forecasting model is well matched to real network traffic, and our links voltage scaling algorithm reduce power consumption of interconnection network effectively.

articleTitle: The Development of Control System in Artificial Heart Valves Test Equipment
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A novel mechanics approach for Artificial heart valves test equipment was developed. The system includes pulsatile pump, accumulator, rectangle cavity, flume, constant temperature device, offspring load and pipelines. The pulsatile pump was designed with piston pump that linear motor drive. Accumulator simulate flexible cavity to change intermittence blood jet into continuous pulsatile flow. This test equipment basically simulated artificial heart valves working condition and system was stabilized. In the heart pump control, the adaptive neural networks controller for a linear motor control system was applied. The proposed controller deals mainly with non-linear disturbances, especially force ripples. The experimental results showed that the neuro controller provides a pronounced improvement in the tracking performance and compensates for the feedback controller imperfection.

articleTitle: Network-based H∞ Control of Systems with Transmission Delays
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper is concerned with an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>control problem for a class of networked control systems (NCSs) with transmission delays, where the delays are time-varying and uncertain. Based on the LMI approach, a new method for designing a memoryless static state feedback control law is proposed to stabilize this class of NCSs and to reduce the effect of the disturbance input on the controlled output to a prescribed level for all admissible transmission delays. The results depend on the solvability of a certain linear matrix inequality and may be less conservative.

articleTitle: Integrated Controller/Detector Design for State-delay Systems Based on Mixed GH2/ H∞ Control
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper considers the integrated controller/detector design problem for time-delay systems with both exogenous disturbance and fault. Using mixed GH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>control theory, the integrated controller/detector is designed. The GH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>norm is considered as a measure for fault detection objectives and the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>norm is considered as a measure for control objectives. The sufficient conditions for the existence of integrated controller/detector and its design method are presented in terms of linear matrix inequality (LMI), independently of time delay. A numerical example is finally given to demonstrate the validity and applicability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Study on the Robot with Limb Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Walking robots with operating capability represent the main direction of future robots development. The limb mechanism, which integrates legged locomotion and arm manipulation, is proposed as a novel design to overcome the operation problems of walking robots. This paper describes the design concepts, analyses and summarizes present development of robots with limb mechanism, and points out some key problems that have to be solved for the robot design

Author Keywords: integrated mechanism of leg and arm

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Ensemble for Land Cover Classification
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Ensemble of artificial neural networks (ANN) often has better performance than any of the single learned ANN in the ensemble. And the combination of remote sensing and geographic ancillary data is believed to offer improved accuracy in land cover classification. However, conventional statistical classifier such as maximum-likelihood classifier (MLC) is not suitable to the ancillary data. In this paper, ANN ensemble is introduced to research on land cover classification. Experimental results show that ANN ensemble has good generalization ability. And classification with combination of remote sensing and geographic ancillary data outperforms single remote sensing data in terms of accuracy. Multisource land cover classification based on ANN ensemble could gain higher classification accuracy.

articleTitle: A New Translation Strategy Based-on Case-Based Reasoning in Machine Translation System
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: To improve machine translation system's translation quality and accurate rate, a case-based reasoning translation strategy was presented. Laying emphasis on the case reasoning part, a structure and semantic similarity algorithm was designed to calculate the sentence similarity. First, a dynamic filter is used to select the translation pattern roughly. Then, based on dynamic programming (DP) algorithm, the structure similarity was decided by the calculation of edit distance. In the process of path recall, an optimization function was defined to select the best matching path. Last, to match the pattern more exactly, the semantic similarity is calculated by the semantic tree structure. The experiment shows that the score of translation quality is 70.11 and the accurate rate can reach 89.4%

articleTitle: A New Practical On-line Equipment to Monitor and Evaluate Fouling and Corrosion of Heat Exchanger
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: To adopt protective measure and guarantee safe and economic operation for heat exchanger, it's necessary to accurate monitor and evaluate fouling and corrosion of heat exchanger. Point at the imperfection of present method to monitor fouling and corrosion of heat exchanger, A new practical on-line equipment was developed based on the soft-measure technology for fouling with easily measured parameters and the mental corrosion rate monitoring technology with the weak polarization method, and introduces mainly the measuring principle, the structure, the performance and the application of the monitoring equipment based on the above principle.

articleTitle: Implementing Automation and Intelligentization of the Talysurf-5 Type Surface Roughness Measuring Instrument
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In order to solve the disadvantages of Talysurf-5 type surface roughness measuring instrument that data processing was slow, printed graphs were inadequate and the operation was tedious, brand-new designs were carried out in the latter circuit and the data processing part, which included hardware circuit design and software programming. Experimental results indicate that the new system has the following features: versatile functions, simple operating and high testing precision, implementing automation and intelligentization of the measurement completely, which has high applicability and performance price ratio

articleTitle: Roulettes of the Fixed Axis Gear Trains and Their Application in Machining Polygon Prisms
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The mathematic model of the roulettes of a fixed axis gear train composed of a couple of gears by transforming coordinates is built firstly, and a series of roulettes are drawn, then the factors which influence their characteristics and shapes are found. The mathematic model of the roulettes of a general fixed axis gear trains is built according to the transmission characteristics of the fixed axis gear train. Parts can be machined to polygon prisms by the property of roulettes that their central shapes are regular polygon prisms if tolerance is permitted. A square is given as an example to analyze error. An experiment and the prototype of its control system are shown in the end

articleTitle: The Nonlinear Adaptive Control for a Class of Based on Dynamic Approximate Higher-Order Nonlinearization
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The adaptive control algorithm, it's parameter adaptive recursive predicting and noise estimator unified form is presented for a class of nonlinear discrete-time systems with multiple time delays based on dynamic approximate any higher-order nonlinearization increment minimized recursive predicting model of NARMAX model(with time delays and noise increment higher-order Volterra model). adaptive control is employed for nonlinear systems with heavy multiple time delays. the simulation result for several typical nonlinear systems are given to demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of approach proposed.

Author Keywords: with time delays and noise increment higher-order Volterra model

articleTitle: Path Following Control for Tractor-Trailer Mobile Robot Based on Virtual Desired Path
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of path following control for tractor-trailer mobile robot (TTMR). Firstly, for several kinds of normal real desired paths (RDP), we design a scheme to construct virtual desired paths (VDP) such that all the bodies of TTMR will array on both sides of the RDP symmetrically and closely when the tractor follows the VDP instead of the RDP. In such a way, the width of the road covered by the whole system will decrease. Secondly, a new control strategy in which the tractor is controlled to follow the VDP is proposed based on the Lyapunov method. The simulation results show the validity and the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of the High Order FIR Multi-Band-Stop Filters
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper traverses the relations between the amplitude-frequency response of FIR filters with the linear phase and the parallel algorithm of neural network, which its activation matrix is H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> - C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup>W , presents and proves the convergence theorem of the neural-network parallel algorithm, and gives the optimal design examples of high order FIR multi-band-stop digital filters. The results show that the parallel algorithm is efficient in the field of optimal design on the high order FIR multi-band-stop digital filters with the linear phase

Author Keywords: High order FIR multi-band-stop digital filters

articleTitle: Online Identification and Control of Guiding System Based on Inverse System
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The nonlinear guiding system is converted into a linear system by integrating inverse system method with parameter identification. Based on a low-order equivalent model, a quasi parallel approaching guiding law is developed from the fast robust adaptive control method. In the system, the angular rate of sight vanishes and the least measurement is needed. Simulating results indicate that the inverse system method is practicable

articleTitle: HIL Simulation of High Altitude Long Endurance UAV's Target Tracking/Flight Integrated Control
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: An integrated modeling and control strategy of payloads platform and flight control system (FCS) is presented for high altitude long endurance unmanned aerial vehicle (HALE UAV). Different from the traditional control method that UAV and payloads platform are modeled and controlled separately, an integrated control idea considering both payloads platform and FCS as a whole is proposed. First, integrated modeling is conducted by deducing the mathematical relation between the payload platform and the UAV's attitude movement. Considering that the UAV platform is usually sensitive to parameter perturbation and external disturbance, robust control theory is then studied and applied in the design of UAV's FCS. A 2-DOF controller containing the disturbance observer (DOB) is designed for payload platform based on the analysis of coupling between the UAV's attitude movement and the payload platform. Finally, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) real-time simulation system for the integrated control of payload platform and FCS is established and simulation results show the effectiveness of the control system.

Author Keywords: high altitude long endurance unmanned aerial vehicle (HALE UAV)
target tracking and flight integrated control system

articleTitle: Study on the Control System of Microarrayer
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The control system is the key parts of microarrayer. The working process and configuration of microarrayer are introduced briefly. Special attention is paid to the analysis and computation method of the working path in microarray fabrication. On the condition of given parameters, such as sample variety, slip quantity, spot matrix module, pin matrix module etc., the working path has been mainly divided into two main subpath, such as Z axis pin path, XY axis spotting path. Then the tree classing method has been taken to calculate the working path with the given parameters. The method and expressions are presented in details. In terms of working path planning of microarrayer, a control system based on LM628 and AC serve driver are implemented successfully. The hardware and software of the system are discussed in details. The agreement of the final computation results with the experimental data indicates the method could be used to estimate the working path of microarrayer quickly and effectively at engineering analyses. The control system are robust and effective

articleTitle: Study on Evaluation of Competition Superiority to Agriculture Plot Based on Fuzzy Optimization Model
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: According to the law of agriculture production, we put forward an superiority evaluation-quota-system of different plots, and build the plot-superiority-evaluation model based on multi-objective system-fuzzy-optimization theory. Several cases on evaluation of competition superiority to agriculture plot are presented to show the difference of each agriculture plot in competition superiority, and provide decision support for production processes. The model can point out the direction of gaining more profits and improving the decision ability for agriculture production.

articleTitle: Study and Stability Analysis on PDC Fuzzy Control System Based on Predictive Controller of T-S Model's Subsystems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A new PDC (parallel distributed compensation) fuzzy control strategy is proposed. This PDC fuzzy control strategy is achieved by applying the State Feedback Predictive Control to each T-S model's subsystem. The stability of the closed loop system is analyzed and two sufficient conditions for global asymptotic stability are given. State feedback model predictive controllers are first developed for the T-S fuzzy model's subsystems. Then in terms of PDC fuzzy control theory, the whole control system's fuzzy control movement can be calculated by each subsystem's control movement and membership function. Finally the fuzzy control movement is used to control the whole system. The inverted pendulum system is also simulated with various initial states. The simulation result shows the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stochastic System Identification Techniques of State Space Models and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The state subspace system identification (4SID) techniques have shown a new approach to the identification of MIMO system. The present paper studied the state subspace system identification method of MIMO system, summarized the advantages of the 4SID techniques, and improved the method of state subspace system identification. Adopted this method, Toeplitz matrix H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>is first identified, and then the state subspace and system parameters matrix are identified. Meanwhile, mathematical demonstration is provided, thus the bottleneck problem of 4SID is solved. Compared with other algorithms, this method bears higher identification precision and practicality.

articleTitle: Contrast-Based Image Fusion in Wavelet Domain
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Wavelet direction contrast based on wavelet multi-resolution and HVS is applied into image fusion. A new fusion scheme is proposed, in which a correlated salience measure function and a normalized correlation measure function for source images are defined while a simple equation for weighed fusion coefficients selection is adopted. Experimental results demonstrate that this improved scheme not only has a better visual effect than former fusion schemes, but also simplifies the computation complexity.

articleTitle: A Fast Recursive Algorithm with Multi-Grade QR Decomposition for Multivariable Transfer Function Matrix Identification
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a fast recursive algorithm with three grade QR decomposition for multi-variable transfer function matrix identification is presented. The algorithm avoids the repeated processing of the measured data of subsystems identification and a parameter estimation that minimizes the overall loss function can be obtained without expanding of parameter vector dimensions. The simulation indicates the validity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Interactive Simulation of Progressive Cutting Model
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Force feedback coupled with visual display allows people to interact intuitively with complex virtual environment. The paper presents a framework for the interactive simulation of surgical cuts. Object deformation is based on mass-spring system and the improved progressive cutting approach is introduced. The paper proposed using BP neural network to calculate the part of haptic force rendering.

articleTitle: Strategy and Experiment of Giant Magnetostrictive Actuator's Orientation Control Based on Preisach Model
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A hysteresis preisach-based numerical model of a reciprocating type GMA (Giant Magnetostrictive Actuator) was established; The problem to calculate preisach converse model directly was solved in the case of static and quasi static state(0∼5Hz) because a real-time numerical compensation algorithm was put forward. The results of orientation control experiments on GMA reveal that a PID plus presiach feedforward compensation control strategy improves the control performance greatly. The maximum error in tracking a 1 Hz varying swing input signal is about third of that obtained using a regular PID controller.

articleTitle: A Study on the Assembly Method of Single Carbon Nanotube Based on Nanomanipulation Robot
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer great potential for the fabrication of nanosystems or nanodevice due to the unique electronic transport properties of the material. However, the most challenging thing to the realization of practical CNT devices could be the formation of reliable and reproducible CNT to metallic contacts. In this work, by using an atomic force microscope (AFM) based nanomanipulate robot, a reliable method is developed to manipulate CNT and make connections between single CNT and electrodes. It is a valuable way for furthering the study of CNT properties and the development of CNT-based nanosystems

articleTitle: Pinning Control of MLW-based Complex Dynamical Networks - Discrete Time Case
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A new complex dynamical network based on multi-local-world (MLW) model is first introduced. Then, control of this kind of complex dynamical network by applying local feedback injections to a tiny fraction of local worlds in the whole network is investigated. Stability conditions are derived for several different dynamical network models including time-invariant networks, time-varying networks and time-delay networks in discrete-time domain respectively. Especially, stabilization of such networks is completely determined by the coupling strength, the inner-coupling matrix, and by the eigenvalues of the coupling configuration matrix and feedback gain matrix.

articleTitle: On-line Monitoring of Penicillin Cultivation Process Based on Multi-way Partial Least Squares
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: On-line monitoring and fault diagnosis of a fed-batch penicillin fermentation process is presented using multi-way partial least squares method (MPLS). Since data from penicillin cultivation process are multidimensional, modeling and fault diagnosis based on the statistical data cannot be realized using traditional partial least squares (PLS) method. Multidimensional data will be cut along the variable axis, PLS model be built for every operational phase using MPLS method, and on-line monitoring and fault diagnosis of batch process be attained. The simulation is performed by means of statistical method such as Hotelling T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Q and contribution plots. From the consistency of theoretical analysis and simulation results, the implementation of the methodology is illustrated.

articleTitle: Optimum Design for Nonlinear Muti-constrained Complex Industrial Process
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The complex industrial process possesses strong nonlinear, muti-constrained, muti-input and muti-output and other characters. It is hard to use the traditional optimization algorithm to resolve the process control optimization problem, which model build by using multiple intelligent techniques. In the paper the method of SUMT is used to transform the muti-target-constrained optimization problem to unlimited optimization problem, the practical Lead-Zinc Sintering Process control model is build by using NN. The parameters optimization is obtained by using the clustering search, elitist preserved simple genetic algorithm and chaos optimization. The whole optimization algorithm possesses the global convergence and effective, better used in practical industrial process.

Author Keywords: Elitist Preserved Simple Genetic Algorithm and Chaos Optimization

articleTitle: Using Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Programming to Evolve Classification Rules
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: According to analyzing particle swarm optimization (PSO), the structure of genetic programming (GP) and classifier model, PSO algorithm and GP were made to combine to evolve classification rules. Rules were described as binary tree which non-leaf node denoted rule structure and leaf-node was correspond to rule value. Leaf node and non-leaf node employed different evolutionary strategy. First, PSO was applied to evolve leaf node in order to obtain the optimum rule of certain structure, then GP was adopted to optimize rule structure. The best rules were obtained after the twice optimization. Finally, the new method indicated efficiency through experiments on several datasets of UCI

articleTitle: The Information Integration Techniques in Automation
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In last 5 to 10 years, great progress has been made in automation in China. A new concept-Comprehensive Automation System-has come into being, which can be simply described as integrating production management systems tightly with process control through various networks. The major characteristic is the synthesis of various techniques and integration of all information within entire enterprise. The main information synthesis techniques which have successfully been applied in metallurgical automation are introduced in the paper, including EIC operation integration, various networkings, MES techniques, etc.

articleTitle: Fundamental Theorem for Optimal Output Feedback Problem with Quadratic Performance Criterion
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The problem of global optimal static output feedback control for linear time-invariant systems with linear quadratic index in the cases of random initial conditions and deterministic initial conditions was investigated. For the given initial condition (the random case), the necessary and sufficient condition—a matrix equation is obtained for the output feedback control to be equal to the optimal state feedback control and in this case, the output feedback is globally optimal. Further, for the deterministic case, the main contribution is to reveal the dependence of the global optimal feedback gain on the given initial condition. All results are described in a linear algebraic equation.

articleTitle: Maximum Torque/Current Control of Hybrid Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the maximum torque/current control of 2-phase hybrid synchronous motor is presented. And at the same time a space-voltage vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) method is put forward based on the 2-phase hybrid synchronous motor driven by H-bridged circuit. Through controlling i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>and i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>respectively, current of the stator windings is utilized more fully and utilization factor of the power supply is raised simultaneously. At last, experiments and simulations of the control system are carried out and results are given.

articleTitle: Observer Design for Nonregular Descriptor Systems with Unknown Inputs in Finite Time
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The problem of inputs decoupled observer design in finite time for nonregular descriptor systems with unknown inputs was considered. Based on the constructive characteristic of the descriptor systems and under some general assumptions, a new nonsingular transformation of the input-state pair of descriptor systems was introduced, which transforms the nonregular descriptor system with unknown inputs into one of standard state-space systems where the inputs were known by regarding the partial state as unknown inputs. The sufficient conditions for the existence of the observer and simple method to design the observer are given, and the state and unknown inputs of the descriptor systems are exactly estimated by the state of observer and output of descriptor systems in finite time

articleTitle: A Novel Bit Rate Allocation Algorithm for Motion JPEG2000
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: An efficient bit rate allocation algorithm for video sequences transmission in Motion JPEG2000 is presented. In many cases, the moving portions of video are often the interested regions. Based on tile encoding of JPEG2000, the important regions are discerned by two parameters. One is complexity of a tile; the other is motion activity of a tile. Thus an adaptive rate-allocation is realized in a lower complexity and the perceptive quality of a frame is improved. Experiments show the effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Random Set Method of Information Fusion under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Information fusion in the presence of uncertainty is an important and intractable problem. Three types of information with uncertainty are represented with random set and the relations of random set theory with fuzzy logic, Dempster-Shafer evidence theory and conditional event algebra are discussed in this paper. Other applications of random set in information fusion are also reviewed. Finally, the future research directions of random set are pointed out

articleTitle: A Hybrid Intelligent Soft-Sensor Method for the Rare Earth Cascade Extraction Process
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The index of element component content is very important in the rare earth cascade extraction process, because it represents the product quality. But it can not be measured online, so that the optimal operation is hardly to be achieved. To deal with the problem, this paper proposes a hybrid intelligent soft-sensor method by combining a bilinear dynamic model with a neural-network-based error compensation model to predict the element component content on-line. Parameters of the default bilinear model and weights of the neural network are first initialized off-line by the least square identification algorithm and the back-propagation algorithm respectively, and then self-tuned on-line when used. Industrial experiments are conducted on a Ce/Pr extraction separation production line of La, Ce, Pr, Nd tetra-component and the results show the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid intelligent soft-sensor method by comparing with data from an industrial locale.

articleTitle: The Data Mining Technique of Time-series Trending Structure Series
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: According to the inner characters of the time series, the conception of time-series trending structure series and the latest time sub-series was defined, and the time-series trending structure mining technique was presented. The technique first converted the time series waiting for mining into its trending structure series, then used the information underlying in the latest trending structure sub-series of the latest time sub-series as a guide to excavate the original time series. The model of RBF neural network was also presented to predict the trend of time series with real world data set. Experimental results reveal that the time-series trending structure mining technique is significant

articleTitle: A Method of Untouched Image Localization for Paper Cutting
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: To seek for new ways of measuring paper cutting to substitute traditional touched measuring methods, an untouched image localization for paper cutting system is proposed in this paper, which makes use of techniques of image segmentation, image match and measurement. The method of image processing in this system is discussed. The precision of the system and the factors that result in measurement errors are analyzed. Experiment results indicate that the measurement time is less than 0.5s, and the precision of measurement is 7mm, which verify the validity of the method. The method provides a new idea for online measurement and localization of objects.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of A DeviceNet Node Interface Based on HCS12D64
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: As a low-level network with its flexibility and openness, DeviceNet is getting more and more applications in field control systems of modern industry. In this paper, a DeviceNet node interface which was Designed and Implemented based on HCS12D64 is introduced. The DeviceNet node interface can be used to connect and communicate a mass of field inspect or control device which has only RS-232C but no DeviceNet interface. Test in laboratory and practical application in a moter protection system shows that the characteristics of the node interface can fully meet the demand of DeviceNet specification. The practical application is successful.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Parallel Architecture for Image Computing
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Algorithms for Image processing and computer vision are natural candidates for high performance computing systems. This paper presents a reconfigurable parallel architecture prototype for image processing base on large scale FPGA computing. The introduced architecture can cover a wide range of real-time computer vision applications from pre-processing operations to low-level interpretation. In order to reduce the memory accessing time and communication latency, prime memory system for neighborhood operations or other data structures and FPGA-based transfer interconnection networks were designed in the introduced prototype system. This proposed architecture allows the user to program the system in both high-lever (soft-programming) and low-level (hard-programming).

articleTitle: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm with Fitness Sharing Based on Rough Sets Theory
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a new method integrated sharing genetic algorithm (SGA), rough sets theory (RST) and bit-climbing algorithm for multimodal function optimization. We apply the SGA to complete the globe search and form niches which indicate the promising locations. Then, we utilize the strong qualitative analysis ability of rough sets to identify these niches. Finally, the bit-climbing algorithm is used to complete the local search and refine the solution in each of niches. The experiment has proved that using this approach to solve the multimodal function optimization is efficient both in robustness and in accuracy

articleTitle: A Fragile Watermarking Scheme For Tamper Detection and Recovery of Image
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A fragile, block-wise, and content-based watermarking scheme for tamper detection and recovery of image is presented. In the scheme, an image is divided into four quadrants firstly. Then correlation groups are set up after some blocks (each size is 8times8) in different two quadrants being matched. Correlative matrix can be got after the blocks of each group correlation operation being processed. This kind of operation is reversible. The watermark which is embedded into the LSB of each block A includes the signature of the block B and a part of correlative matrix of the two blocks B. The block A and block B should be in relatively long distance in image. The advantage of the scheme is that the tamper content is recovered by untampered content. The experimental results show that our scheme can be applied in detecting and localizing any tampering of equal or more than the size of 8times8 pixels. The recovery of the tampered image is better than that of the scheme of Fridrich et al. (1999)

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Wireless Local Area Network Based on Improved Adaptive Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Locating access point (AP) and achieving wireless network covering with the fewest access points is a difficult research point in the wireless local area network (WLAN) design. The cost of organizing WLAN can be reduced effectively if the problem is resolved. Based on analyzing the transmission model of WLAN, a new optimized model was built. The improved adaptive genetic algorithm (IAGA) was introduced at the same time. It is able to optimize multi-objective constrained problem and determine the distribution of each AP of WLAN. Through computing the examples, the simulation result displays the efficiency of the scheme evidently

articleTitle: Study on constant-tension Control of Rolling Machine Based on Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The new approach of the constant-tension control of rolling machine is presented in this paper, On the premise of the close-loop control of the induction motor torque, the torque of the induction motor can adjust along with the change of the rolling machine diameter automatically, so the constant-tension control is realized. The rotor speed signal adopted in the system is derived from the indirect measurement based on induction motor theory. The approach employs recursive least squares (RLS) to estimate rotor speed in real time. The accuracy of estimated rotor speed is independent of rotor resistance's value. The results show that the system has good static performance. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is approved.

articleTitle: Partial Parallel Interference Cancellation Multiuser Detection using Recurrent Neural Network Based on Hebb Learning Rule
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: In CDMA communication systems, in order to decrease the influence on reception performance resulted from incorrect decision of the interference users' information bits in parallel interference cancellation (PIC) process, a recurrent neural network based on Hebb learning rule is designed and applied to adjusting interference cancellation factors (ICF) in partial parallel interference cancellation (PPIC) multiuser detection. Simulation results show that the proposed Hebb-PPIC detection has strong anti-MAI ability and its performance of bit error rate (BER) is improved on the basis of conventional PIC in both conditions of ideal power control and "near-far" scenario.

articleTitle: Solving Finite Word Length Realization Problems in the Framework of Structured Singular Value
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Based on the structured singular value theory, a tractable stability measure is derived for controllers/filters with the finite word length implementation consideration. The optimal realizations of controllers/filters are defined as those that maximize this measure. A sophisticated optimization strategy is presented to provide an efficient method for solving this problem based on the linear matrix inequality, and a numerical example is given to illustrate the design procedure.

articleTitle: Hybrid Output Feedback Stabilization for a Harmonic Oscillating System
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid static output feedback stabilization approach for harmonic oscillating systems, which are not stabilizable via a static output feedback. More precisely, we find two output feedback gains and a switching law orchestrating the feedback gains such that the closed-loop system is asymptotically stable. It is shown that stability conditions can be met with respect to the discrete state when the switched system's stabilization theorem is used.

articleTitle: On-line Monitoring of Batch Processes Using Kalman Filter and Multivariate Statistical Methods
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Multiway principal component analysis (MPCA) has been implemented to batch process monitoring widely and effectively. In general, when applying MPCA method for on-line monitoring, the unknown future data from the current time until the end of the batch have to be estimated, but it is always difficult to foresee the future behaviour precisely. In this paper, a novel method is proposed by using Kalman filter to recursively estimate the complete state of process and then using MPCA to detect abnormal batch runs. Effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on a simulated benchmark fed-batch penicillin fermentation process.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Diagnosis for Nonlinear System Based on Neural Network on-line Approximator
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: A fault detection and diagnosis method based on neural networks on-line approximation structure for nonlinear system with uncertainties was presented. The approximator, which was realized by radial basis function networks, was used for learning the nonlinear fault functions to monitor the abnormal behavior of dynamic system. When faults occured, the on-line approximator could not only detect all possible unknown faults, but also estimate the faults vector. By the definition of dead area function, it was proved that the scheme had good robustness against modeling error and uncertainties. At last, the simulations and experiment results of a three-tank system illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method

articleTitle: Advanced Process Control System for the Rectification of Vinyl Chloride
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The characteristic of process and control for the rectification of Vinyl Chloride Monomer (VCM) is analyzed. Based on the predictive functional control, the total solution of advanced process control for the rectification of VCM is proposed for solving the control difficulty. Using the predictive functional control virtues sufficiently in fast tracking speed, strong disturbance rejection performance and good robustness, the solution improves the smoothness of the key parameters for process, assures the quality of VCM and retains the smoothness of process. The results of application show that the advanced process system can bring about more economic benefits for the rectification of VCM.

articleTitle: Multiple Models Fuzzy Control for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: It is difficult to obtain satisfied control result using traditional adaptation control of parameters change of model in different operating modes. Combined fuzzy theory and multiple models control, a fuzzy multiple models control algorithm was presented. First of all, sub-models and corresponding controllers were established at each equilibrium point of the system, and then through online each model matching degree was calculated to accommodate parameters change. Finally, the input of the system was a weighted sum of each controller's output. The close-loop system stability can be guaranteed. The simulation results show that the control scheme greatly improves the system dynamic response.

articleTitle: Landmark Recognition System for Mini Rotor Aerial Robot
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Landmark recognition system is a very important part of mini rotor aerial robot. It recognizes landmarks, and supplies the navigation computer with location information of it. However, mini rotor aerial robots have low pay-load and are small in size. This means that the sensor like radar not fit in with this application and the small size and low power cost cameras may be the only sensors can be used. In this paper we focus on a landmark recognition system which uses an onboard camera as the sensor. Meanwhile, this paper presents an approach that is applied to real-time recognizing of landmark in video stream. This problem poses several challenges. Landmark in images captured from video stream by moving mini rotor robot vary in shape, size, scale and orientation. Unlike other approaches, this approach is based on classification algorithms. An extended set of Haar-like features is used, due to their simplicity. Landmarks are divided into several viewpoint categories according to their poses and each of these categories is processed by a cascade classifier which is trained by the Adaboosting algorithm. In the end, the experimental results verify the effectiveness of the system

articleTitle: Application of Stochastic Approximation to Digital Knowledge Products Pricing in Electronic Commerce
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: It is very difficult to price thousands of digital knowledge products (DKP) dynamically reflecting all the products' characteristics and constraints by traditional pricing in electronic commerce. To solve this problem, we adopted a combined model approach that selected appropriate pricing models and integrated them. The three proposed models are cost-plus, customer-expectation and customer-consumption models. We adopted stochastic approximation to set weight. In particular, we considered the case in which automatic pricing was done in order to maximize the profit and the number of sale of an on-line marketing site. We described the concrete pricing algorithms, and reported on preliminary performance evaluation of experiments. The results of experimentation verify that our methods are practical in terms of both the speed of convergence to the optimal price and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Zero Phase Error Robust Controller Design Based on Neural Compensation
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Using the future desired input value, zero phase error controller makes the overall system's frequency response exhibit zero phase shift for all frequencies and a small gain error at low frequency range, which presents a new algorithm to design the feedforward controller. However, zero phase error controller is only suitable for certain system. In order to reduce the phase error and improve robustness, the design of proposed feedforward controller uses a neural compensation based on diagonal recurrent neural network. Simulation results for a servo system show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Hotelling's Competition for Price and Location of Elasticity Demand Product
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Based on Hotelling model, this paper studies the optimal strategies of location and price for elastic demand product whose unit transportation cost can be neglected. According to the location and price of two surrounding enterprises, the core enterprise's making optimal strategies program can be divided into three models, and each model includes several situations. We get the optimal solution for each situation. Based on this, the global optimal strategies for each model are found. Using the result, a universal way for enterprise's making optimal strategies of price and location is given. Finally, using numeric simulation, the result is confirmed to be right and helpful for enterprise

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control for Uncertain Nonholonomic Systems in Chained Form
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The problems of almost asymptotic stabilization and global asymptotic regulation (GAR) are considered by using output feedback for a class of uncertain nonholonomic systems. By combining the nonsmooth change of coordinates and output feedback domination design together, we construct a simple linear time-variable output feedback controller, which can universally stabilizes a whole family of uncertain nonholonomic systems. The simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Computing Service Platform Architecture
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The development of network technology and parallel computation provides dramatically opportunity for complicate Optimization Computing Research. This paper brings forward the concept of Optimization Computing Service, which is the theoretic foundation for designing the framework of Optimization Computing Service Platform—MetaSolver. MetaSlover consist of User Interface, Storage Service, Monitor, Dispatcher, Executor etc. Multiple solvers and multiple tasks could be scheduled and executed cooperatively and efficiently based on dynamic load balance algorithm and its implementation is detailed. Numerical experiments conducted on MetaSolver, which are applied to different fields, demonstrates that the Optimization Computing Service Platform is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Robust Motion Control of High Precision Mechanical Servo Systems with Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: When implementing different tasks, mechanical servo systems must adapt to various working loads with different weight or inertia, which may lead to the remarkable varying of inertial parameters. However, for such cases, motion control methods at present such as PD control and disturbance observer based robust control design, may exhibit instability or decline of tracking performance. For the problems mentioned above, a novel nonlinear control scheme, for which the varying range of inertial parameters was supposed to known, was presented. The nonlinear controller is composed of two parts: the PD control design for the reference model system, and the sliding mode control of the mechanical plant. The sliding mode technique was used for servo system to achieve robust stability and guaranteed transient response, and the boundary layer control was adopted to avoid chattering introduced by control switching. The global stability of the system is proved, and the transient performance is analyzed. Computer simulation results developed for a DC motor servo system show the effectiveness of the proposed method

articleTitle: An Approach to Estimate Robot Pose under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Estimating robot pose accurately is a key problem in incremental mapping for unknown environment, because there are uncertain information both in the map that has been partially built and in the data from sensors. This paper proposes an algorithm for pose estimation under those uncertainty based on Cox algorithm, which reckons robot pose with the requirement that the map is totally known and exact. The way matching an image to a model is used to get a rude correspondence between the sensor data and the half-baked map. Then removing improper matching and employing weighted matrix are applied to reduce the impact of data's and map's error. The refined pose is estimated by weighted least square with the best congruence. In addition, the error resulted from pseudocongruence are resolved by adding virtual lines and dots. Experimental results from actual runs demonstrate that our approach is well suited for pose estimation under uncertainty.

articleTitle: Output Tracking Control for a Class of Time-Delay Systems using Variable Structure Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Based on fuzzy Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) model and variable structure control technique, the output tracking control problem for fuzzy time-delay systems in the existence of parameter perturbations is developed. Firstly, the sliding mode is chosen by variable structure control theory. According to reaching condition, the variable control method was proposed on condition that the time delay is precisely available and unavailable, respectively. The method guaranteed the trajectory of system to arrive the slide surface in finite time interval and be kept here thereafter. Secondly, the sufficient condition for globally bound of the state is proposed by using Input to state systems (ISS) theory and linear matrix inequality (LMI) method. Finally, simulation example is employed to illustrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Optimal Color Image Fusion Approach Based on Quantitative Evaluation Indexes
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: The fusion technology of multi-sources images is important for spatial information applications, such as digital city. In order to keep the spectral information and spatial information in the process of multi-sources spatial images fusion, an optimal image fusion method based on quantitative evaluation indexes is proposed in this paper. In IHS (intensity, hue and saturation) transform space, the feature image of high frequency of intensity component I is fused with multi-resolution wavelet. And the low frequency of intensity component I is fused on pixel level with optimal weight coefficients. Spectral information index E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SP</sub> and spatial resolution index AG are used to adjust the fusion rule and achieve the optimum weight. The test results with QuickBird data show the effectiveness of presented method

articleTitle: Availability Modeling and Simulating of Redundant Hot-standby Control System using Stochastic Reward Nets
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
abstract: Availability model should be introduced to estimate system behavior in the field of redundant hot-standby controller design in integrated automation systems of process industry. Stochastic Reward Nets (SRN) model was established based on two-node hot-standby computers on process automaton level. Both RAID share and mirror share were addressed in the study and data was simulated and analyzed using SPNP package. With SRN model, multidimensional availability parameters can be operated accurately and flexibly during the whole pipeline design, which apparently preponderate over the ability of traditional Markov model and combine model. The method can also be exploited for the development of more general modeling on fundamental automation level.

articleTitle: Neural Network Predictive Control Based on Particle Swarm Optimization for Urban Expressway
publicationTitle: 2006 6th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation
